must_remember: Every body above absolute zero ($0\text{ K}$) emits and absorbs thermal radiation simultaneously.
Thermal radiations are electromagnetic waves traveling at the speed of light in vacuum and do not require any medium.

Kirchhoff's Law states that the ratio of emissive power to absorptive power for any given wavelength is constant for all bodies at the same temperature and equals the emissive power of a black body ($E/a = E_b$).
Stefan-Boltzmann Law relates emissive power of a black body to absolute temperature as $E = \sigma T^4$.
Newton's Law of Cooling is an approximation valid only for small temperature differences between a body and its surroundings, stating rate of cooling is proportional to temperature difference.

glossary.meaning: Total amount of radiant energy emitted per unit time per unit surface area for a specific wavelength interval.
The ratio of radiant energy absorbed by a body to the total radiant energy incident upon it.
An idealized body that absorbs all incident radiation of all wavelengths falling on it, having absorptivity $a = 1$.
The ratio of the emissive power of a real body to the emissive power of a black body at the same temperature.
The product of the absolute temperature $T$ and the wavelength of maximum emission $\lambda_m$, which is a constant.
